propositions: After rebasing onto current origin/main, runner.py is 713 LOC and the test_runner_regains_real_headroom_under_the_cap test fails because the split no longer lands under the attested <700 target.
The failure is due to baseline drift: main grew runner.py to 798 LOC (near the 800 cap), so replaying 2682's split now yields 713 instead of the originally attested 655.

The candidate seams (_import_pydantic_ai, _pai_check_config, _check_tool_capability/_TOOL_CAPABILITY_CHECKED) are pinned as monkeypatch seams across ~15 test sites, so they cannot be moved without many test edits.

The chosen resolution extracts _import_pydantic_ai and _pai_check_config from runner.py into structured_run.py, reducing runner.py to 680 LOC with zero test edits by re-importing the seams as module globals.
Re-deriving the target or adding a re-export shim to mechanically pass the cap were rejected as altering a closed story's attested criterion or violating the module-size policy.
The full suite passes on the rebased stack (8143 passed, 0 failed) with lint and typecheck clean, corroborated by CI on change 1081.
